headline: Lumax Auto Technologies seeks shareholder approval for loans, guarantees and securities up to ₹500 cr under Section 185, Companies Act
sum: Lumax Auto Technologies' board approved a proposal to seek shareholder consent for advancing loans, providing guarantees and security up to ₹500 cr under Section 185 of the Companies Act, 2013. The move, recommended by the Audit Committee, will be placed before the shareholders at the next general meeting.
implication: Section 185 advance-approval frameworks allow boards to act flexibly on inter-company credit without obtaining shareholder consent for each transaction, provided aggregate exposure remains within the pre-approved ceiling and all statutory safeguards (Audit Committee review, arm's-length pricing, full disclosure) are observed.
detail: Lumax Auto Technologies Limited informed the NSE that its Board, in a meeting on 29 May 2026, approved a proposal to secure shareholder approval for providing loans, guarantees and security up to ₹500 crores under Section 185 of the Companies Act, 2013. The Audit Committee had previously recommended this blanket approval, which is a standard governance practice enabling the company to deploy working capital and provide inter-company credit within a pre-approved envelope without repeated shareholder resolutions. The proposal will be tabled at the shareholders' general meeting for formal consent.

framework.note: central; governs loans, guarantees and securities by a company to directors, key managerial personnel, and entities in which they have interest; shareholder approval required for any loan/guarantee/security above threshold; board may seek blanket advance approval within a ceiling
central; prescribes composition and role of Audit Committee; mandatory review of related-party transactions, loans and guarantees before board approval

central; defines Material Related Party Transactions (RPTs); transactions above threshold require Audit Committee and shareholder approval; Section 185 loans/guarantees are RPT-adjacent and may trigger § 188 disclosures
central; mandates RPT disclosures, Audit Committee approval and shareholder ratification for material RPTs; applies to listed companies like Lumax

amended; requires disclosure of loans, advances, guarantees and securities given under Section 185 in the Board's Report; recent amendments tightened related-party and contingent-liability disclosures
central; mandates detailed disclosure in the Notice of General Meeting for all related-party matters requiring shareholder approval; Section 185 proposals must include purpose, terms, board rationale

framework.note: central; exchange-level governance rule requiring advance disclosure and approval framework for listed entities' RPTs and loans to related parties

structure.novel: Advance-approval framework under Section 185 is standard practice but allows board discretion to deploy capital for inter-company lending/guarantees within the ₹500 cr envelope without requiring a fresh shareholder resolution for each transaction.

triggers.note: Any loan, advance, guarantee or security by a listed company to related parties or for acquisition of shares/securities requires shareholder approval; ceiling-based advance approval is permitted
Related-party transactions and loans by listed entities must be disclosed to the exchange and shareholders; Audit Committee approval mandatory
All Section 185 loans and guarantees must be disclosed in the Directors' Report with counterparty, amount, tenure and business rationale
Stock exchange-level requirement for immediate disclosure to NSE of board/shareholder decisions on related-party credit facilities
